content: The data provided outlines exposure scenarios and associated risks for various manufactured nanomaterials (MNMs) during different industrial processes. 1. Spraying and Finishing Processes: High Exposure: Inhalation exposure was observed in 10 cases, with 1 simulation study. Dermal exposure was noted in 44 cases for carbon nanotubes (CNTs) and carbon nanofibres (CNFs), 10 cases for silicon-based materials, 12 cases for titanium dioxide (TiO2), and 13 cases for other metal oxides and mixtures. There were 25 cases for other MNMs, with 2 simulation studies. Inhalation exposure for other MNMs was recorded in 1 case, with 3 simulation studies. Medium Exposure: Inhalation exposure was recorded in 4 cases for CNTs and CNFs, 12 cases for silicon-based materials, 20 cases for TiO2, and 12 cases for other metal oxides and mixtures. Dermal exposure was noted in 23 cases for other MNMs, with 8 cases for other materials. Low Exposure: Inhalation exposure was observed in 1 case for CNTs and CNFs, 2 cases for silicon-based materials, 12 cases for TiO2, and 25 cases for other metal oxides and mixtures. Dermal exposure was recorded in 36 cases for other MNMs, with 14 cases for other materials. 2. Feeding into a Process: High Exposure: Inhalation exposure was recorded in 6 cases for CNTs and CNFs, with 3 simulation studies. Dermal exposure was noted in 26 cases for silicon-based materials, 8 cases for TiO2, and 3 cases for other MNMs, with 6 simulation studies. Medium Exposure: Inhalation exposure was observed in 1 case for CNTs and CNFs, 4 cases for silicon-based materials, and 25 cases for TiO2. Dermal exposure was recorded in 2 cases for other MNMs. Low Exposure: Inhalation exposure was noted in 3 cases for CNTs and CNFs, 2 cases for silicon-based materials, and 1 case for TiO2. Dermal exposure was recorded in 6 cases for other MNMs. 3. Testing and Characterization: High Exposure: Inhalation exposure was observed in 3 cases for CNTs and CNFs, with 1 simulation study. Dermal exposure was recorded in 31 cases for silicon-based materials, 17 cases for TiO2, and 5 cases for other MNMs, with 1 simulation study. Medium Exposure: Inhalation exposure was noted in 2 cases for CNTs and CNFs, and dermal exposure was recorded in 33 cases for other MNMs. Low Exposure: Inhalation exposure was observed in 2 cases for CNTs and CNFs, 1 case for silicon-based materials, and dermal exposure was recorded in 23 cases for other MNMs. 4. Extrusion/Injection Moulding: High Exposure: Inhalation exposure was recorded in 2 cases for CNTs and CNFs, with 3 simulation studies. Dermal exposure was noted in 4 cases for silicon-based materials, 5 cases for TiO2, and 1 case for other MNMs, with 6 simulation studies. Medium Exposure: Inhalation exposure was observed in 1 case for CNTs and CNFs, and dermal exposure was recorded in 25 cases for other MNMs. Low Exposure: Inhalation exposure was noted in 1 case for silicon-based materials, and dermal exposure was recorded in 23 cases for other MNMs. 5. Packing: High Exposure: Inhalation exposure was recorded in 1 case for CNTs and CNFs, and dermal exposure was noted in 114 cases for silicon-based materials, 50 cases for TiO2, and 16 cases for other MNMs. Medium Exposure: Inhalation exposure was observed in 2 cases for CNTs and CNFs, and dermal exposure was recorded in 66 cases for other MNMs. Low Exposure: Inhalation exposure was noted in 1 case for CNTs and CNFs, and dermal exposure was recorded in 7 cases for other MNMs. 6. Total Exposure: Across all activities, the total number of inhalation exposure cases was 163 for CNTs and CNFs, 147 for silicon-based materials, 42 for TiO2, 38 for other metal oxides and mixtures, and 43 for other MNMs. Dermal exposure cases totaled 371 across all materials. 7. Key Definitions: CNTs: Carbon Nanotubes. CNFs: Carbon Nanofibres. MNMs: Manufactured Nanomaterials. Si-based: Silicon-based materials. TiO2: Titanium Dioxide. 8. Additional Notes: The likelihood of dermal and/or ingestion exposure is considered equal in the cases marked with a. The number of simulation studies conducted is provided in parentheses. This detailed breakdown provides a comprehensive understanding of the exposure scenarios and associated risks for various nanomaterials during specific industrial processes.
